SOAP Clinical Note

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Cough and cold symptoms for approximately 5 days.
- History of presenting complaint:
  - Onset: Started at the beginning of the weekend (approx. 5 days ago).
  - Symptoms: Dry (non-productive) cough, runny nose, muscle aches, occasional headache, chills.
  - Denies shortness of breath, wheeze, chest rattling noises, or hemoptysis.
- Past medical history: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (diagnosed ~5-6 years ago), hypertension (on antihypertensive medication).
- Medications:
  - Metformin (dose/route/frequency not documented)
  - Lisinopril (dose/route/frequency not documented)
  - Paracetamol (as needed, dose/route/frequency not documented)
- Social history: Not documented.
- Allergies: Not documented.

Objective:
- Reported well-controlled blood glucose at home (no abnormal readings).
- Reported blood pressure this morning was within normal range (specific values not recalled).
- Oropharyngeal examination: Mild redness at the back of throat, no tonsillar enlargement.
- No palpable cervical lymphadenopathy (per patient’s self-exam).
- No other examination findings documented.
- No investigations performed or documented.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute upper respiratory tract infection ("cough and cold"):
   - Assessment: Likely viral upper respiratory tract infection.
   - Differential diagnosis: Not documented.
   - Investigations: None indicated at this time.
   - Treatment:
     - Supportive care advised: symptomatic treatment with over-the-counter Night Nurse or Day Nurse (safe with current medications).
     - Continue regular medications.
   - Safety netting:
     - Advised to seek medical attention if symptoms worsen (e.g., development of shortness of breath, wheeze, or prolonged symptoms beyond three weeks), or become generally unwell.

Quality checks:

● Missing elements:
  - Allergies not documented.
  - Complete social history not documented.
  - Dose/route/frequency of all medications not documented.
  - No review of other systems or of past infectious episodes.
● Internal conflicts:
  - None identified.
● Transcript quality:
  - Clear transcript, no significant inaudible sections.
